requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request any implementation source.

- **`/`-separated path and empty selector selects root.**
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` parses multi-segment selectors, and parses `""` to an empty segment list.
  - It rejects malformed input such as `a//b`, `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]` and `fn[run]x`.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts `outline.resolve("") == 0`. It also resolves nested selectors such as `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and each resolved node's `selector` equals the selector used.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` resolves a path that goes through an anonymous node, `pair[items]/item@…/pair[f]`.
- **Named segment is `kind[name]`.** The Rust selector tests assert the exact generated selectors. They include `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `extern[C]`, `extern[Rust]` and `extern-crate[core]`.
- **Anonymous segment is `kind@` plus the first 12 hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts the `use@` prefix and a total length of `use@` plus 12.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` asserts the selector equals `pair[items]/item@{identity_hash[..12]}`. It also asserts that identity_hash differs from structural_hash, and that editing a descendant leaves the selector unchanged.
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` checks that the hash label is normalized to lowercase.
- **`#N` disambiguation by one-based source order.**
  - `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` asserts `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2`. It checks that `#1` is the first declaration in the file, and that swapping the declarations swaps the ordinals.
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` and `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` assert `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`.
  - The bare ambiguous `fn[repeated]` fails to resolve.
  - The anonymous case is covered by two identical `use` items getting `#1` and `#2`. `#0` is rejected by the parser test.
- **`line` nodes are exempt, and any line with that content resolves.** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` asserts that the identical lines `alpha` and `alpha` get equal `line@` selectors with no `#N`. It also asserts that the selector resolves, and that the `beta` line is distinct. It checks that whitespace is ignored within a line's hash (`two  words` matches `two words`) while `twowords` differs.
- **Percent-encoding.**
  - `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` encodes a name containing space, `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`, `%` and tab. The name also contains a non-breaking space and an ideographic space, which are Unicode whitespace.
  - The test asserts the exact encoded output as UTF-8 bytes, leaves `é` unencoded, and checks the decode round trip. It rejects raw `/`, a bad escape and raw whitespace.
  - The `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` selectors show the encoding applied in generated selectors.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` prepends blank lines. It asserts the selectors are unchanged while `line_start` shifts from 1 to 4.

I found no gap. The hash computation itself belongs to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which I did not reassess. No {fixme} acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
